proposed_from.topic: Incremental joint constant-score-span GMM weighting and pointwise inference for a prespecified aggregate of covariate-adjusted staggered DDD effects when multiple admissible comparison cohorts share units. The note takes the published Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna pairwise scores as a fixed retained score vector, identifies the causal aggregate, constructs an everywhere-defined clipped, projected, and ridged cross-fitted estimator conditional on supplied L4 nuisance rates and a product-rate condition, and compares joint covariance weighting with separate within-block optimization. Its contribution is the DDD-specific shared-cell covariance mapping, the exact if-and-only-if equality frontier and quadratic variance gap, a feasible descriptive loss diagnostic, and a bounded open nonzero-effect strict-gap family. Hsieh's shared-unit covariance accounting and generic finite-dimensional GMM/SUR quadratic algebra are prior art and are not claimed as new. The scope is pointwise and finite dimensional: no full conditional-moment efficient influence function or semiparametric efficiency bound, uniform learner attainability or coverage, or covariate-varying relative-precision result is claimed.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level target is Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's componentwise optimal GMM. The new field-specific object is the full DDD incidence-constrained system for the final scalar aggregate, which permits zero-sum comparison contrasts from other blocks; generic constrained-GMM algebra itself is not claimed as novel. The exact frontier \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\) and its DDD shared-cell covariance expansion isolate when the published plug-in aggregation loses information. The open classification is posed over a sufficient invariant carrying score and comparison labels, cohort-eligibility-time residual labels, signed incidences, \(\omega\), the compatible covariance map, and canonical \(N\), rather than an unlabelled graph. Hsieh already handles cross-stack dependence for inference, but does not optimize across multiple admissible comparison-cohort scores or state the joint-versus-separate frontier.

seed_details.kernel: Derive the EIF and semiparametric bound for the full pairwise conditional staggered-DDD moment model.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie because DDD is merely a difference of DiDs.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their moment system has no eligibility-domain contrast and no DDD shared-comparison residual covariance; Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna explicitly name overidentified DDD efficiency as future work.

seed_details.anchor: OrtizVillavicencioSantAnna2025, staggered GMM construction; ChenSantAnnaXie2025, conditional weighting discussion
seed_details.kernel: Give necessary and sufficient covariance-row-space conditions for constant comparison weights to be efficient.
seed_details.red_team: It is tautological to say fixed weights fail when optimal weights vary with covariates.
seed_details.rebuttal: The surviving version states the primitive equivalence \(\Sigma(X)^{-1}\mathbf1\parallel\overline\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1\) and a positive quadratic variance gap with shared-unit covariance.

seed_details.anchor: AkbariKiyavashGhassami2025, estimation section and conclusion; ChernozhukovEtAl2018
seed_details.kernel: Prove uniform cross-fitted attainment with regularized conditional covariance inversion.
seed_details.red_team: Routine DML once an EIF is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: The non-routine part is establishing orthogonality and controlling the extra inverse-covariance nuisance under reused comparison cohorts; it is retained only as an attainment theorem paired with S1.

seed_details.anchor: OrtizVillavicencioSantAnna2025, event-study aggregation; ChenSantAnnaXie2025, event-study EIF
seed_details.kernel: Characterize when separately GMM-optimal group-event estimators are globally efficient for a scalar event-study aggregate.
seed_details.red_team: A linear aggregate of efficient components is automatically efficient.
seed_details.rebuttal: That implication fails if component scores were optimized in separate restricted classes; shared units induce cross-cell covariance absent from pointwise GMM.

seed_details.anchor: ChenSantAnnaXie2025, Hausman and incremental Sargan discussion
seed_details.kernel: Derive a limit law for a test of conditional-GLS collapse in staggered DDD.
seed_details.red_team: A standard Hausman test already does this.
seed_details.rebuttal: A new test would require nonparametric conditional covariance estimation, but it is secondary until the DDD EIF exists.

seed_details.kernel: Find a minimax rate for estimating the conditional covariance weight under smoothness.
seed_details.red_team: The rate depends entirely on an arbitrary smoothness class and is detached from the causal target.
seed_details.rebuttal: No natural regime parameter arises from the supplied DDD gap, so this candidate is dropped.

seed_details.kernel: Choose comparison cohorts to optimize a policy objective.
seed_details.red_team: Comparison-cohort choice is an estimator choice, not a treatment-assignment policy.
seed_details.rebuttal: The target is a fixed ATT aggregate, so the M16 lane has no credible seed in this substrate.

seed_details.kernel: Invert a placebo permutation test for a DDD event-study aggregate.
seed_details.red_team: Observational staggered panels lack the exact exchangeability needed for permutation validity.
seed_details.rebuttal: No credible symmetry group follows from the maintained model, so the M17 lane is dropped rather than padded.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel survives against four adjacent threads: canonical DDD EIFs in Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025); pairwise staggered-DDD DR/GMM in Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025); overidentified staggered two-way DiD EIFs in Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025); and the sequential conditional-moment efficiency geometry of Ai and Chen (2012). Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020) supplies the just-identified DiD benchmark. None contains both the eligibility-domain DDD residual and the multi-cohort conditional covariance projection.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-system-limit and thm:separate-joint-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Optimality is confined to constant loadings in the fixed retained vector of pairwise DDD scores; it is not the semiparametric efficiency bound of the full conditional-moment DDD model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The accepted field claim is feasible joint score-span GMM inference and its joint-versus-componentwise frontier for fixed T, retained comparisons, and prespecified aggregate weights.
